"credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "毕业后2011年在新加坡留学期间在东南亚各地旅行的经历也似乎对作家来说也是一个重要的经历:温暖多湿的热带气候的植物,看起来非常活力,其群生,森林,现在被其迫力所压倒。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对植物的兴趣一直是福本的灵感来源,似乎有与植物的相遇,随时触摸,学生时代,在艺术大附近的上野、谷中樱桃散落后,新绿叶在头上重重,从这个间隔落下,被光包围的感觉,在心中留下了强烈的感觉。 2011 去年在新加坡留学期间,在东南亚各地旅行的经历也似乎对作家来说也是一个重要的经历。高温多潮湿的热带气候的植物非常活力,似乎已经被其群生和森林的迫力所吸引,2018年,他作为作家参加了在奥基纳本岛北部举行的“努力艺术节2018-2019”。如今,福本每天都通往小石川植物园,被植物激发。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "被森林所吸引的画家", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于植物和画家来说,17世纪的内德兰特花的静态画很快被记住,从18世纪末到19世纪的英国中心的精确植物画,许多画家成为创造植物的生命力的目标。在日本说,植物学家牧野富太郎自己的绘画,继续绘制 ⁇ 美大岛的自然和植物的田中一村,以及从自己的角度夺取植物生命的井文子等,有画家深深地进入植物生态。关于森林,也没有提及德国浪漫主义的卡斯珀·达维特·弗里德里希、卡米尤·科洛和巴尔维森派画家、东山魁夷等。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/a1bb364b/859f94ab-8d0c-4205-99d5-e7e6e9a18cf9.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 安静的旋律 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "只是福本的创作引发了作者的记忆,这些是与异性施尔莱主义周围的几位画家的存在,例如,马克斯·埃尔恩斯特将德国线区的荒凉森林的童年体验作为其终身灵感的源头,他多次试图创造一个图像,产生荒凉森林景观的神秘氛围。艾伦斯特用自己想象的绘画技巧格拉塔吉(将无缝的画具放在<unk>的材料上,用板刀等切割,在屏幕上画出独特的品质感的技巧)描绘了这件神秘的作品。显然,西勒主义后期画家和来自古巴的维弗雷德·拉姆也被称为被家乡热带雨林所吸引的画家,与西方人不同起源的故乡形象的武器,通过与西勒主义者的交流培养的方法(特别是称为“美丽的尸体(卡达尔·埃克斯基)”,不受现有概念和理性,而偶然出生。多用奇怪天外图像创造的方法)等,描绘了植物与生物团结的幻觉空间,第二次世界大战后在巴黎活跃的德国画家沃尔斯的存在也想象。沃尔斯所描绘的植物和树木等动机不是自然的重现,而是生命的根源、内在的奇迹、宇宙形象的独特描述。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/fa41946b/de0b75ca-d18b-4e1f-991c-5233d2f4d580.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 阿姆伯的时间 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "听到这些对画家的兴趣,关于弗里德里希和艾伦斯特,从前已经重复了画集,但从来没有直接有意识地制作过,但是画家对植物和其群体的兴趣,或被激励,并继续保持这种感觉的态度似乎可以看到作为艺术家的品质一致。福本在植物、森林、近年来细胞和微生物等自然界各个对象寻求灵感来源,向自己的绘画晋升。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/803e0800/788dce65-556b-4cdd-b90c-93c07318c704.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 阿姆伯的时间(部分) 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "偶然一滴的世界", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览的标题取决于作家本人的名称,这是从长田弘(1939年至2015年)的诗作中获得的想象,长田是福岛的编辑和诗人,有诗作如《人曾经是树》(2006)、《世界是顺利》(2009)等。被偶然的纳加达的言语所吸引,拿起诗集的福本与纳加达的作品分享了从可忽视的小东西到大东西的传播感;福本的创作始于将油画工具一滴倒在坎巴斯上;自己内心的形象和偶然的一滴传播的世界;与自己的创造有关的自然中发现的小东西无限地传播的感觉,重重于诗人的言语。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "福本在制作程序中,在各个方面都具有独特性;支持体的制作也是自己做的,制作木框,粘贴滑板,地下地点做的也是画家自己做的;用水彩画的技巧获得的感觉多用,重重画具的层,创造后行,在其上自由散布生物摩尔形状,这些创造也是独特的。探讨生产过程中产生的形状和变化,同时试图创造超越自己的理性和意图的意外偶然组合和无意识的形象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/db6edb6d/66d1164a-61c1-47a1-a02d-d39688b53a56.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 光的余白(部分) 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在图像的创造中,福本这一次多用的是绘画工具的“输入(绘画工具流)”技术,“输入”是现代作家中,具体艺术协会的前永定正的代表性技术,先前意识到组成,倾向转动,在那里油画工具缓慢滴流,画家的控制和重力による偶然结合。因此,它将充满生命力的有机品质感带到屏幕上;在地下画的坎巴斯上,一滴绘画工具,如倾斜、流动、渗透、冲动等,随机性利用,随机性利用,同时在自己的创作企图中成功地插入偶然,屏幕的表情会多样地展开,甚至是愚蠢的,形成一个广阔的空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/616d277c/b744548d-7c05-402f-bb81-5c52bfe0fda0.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 安静之环(部分) 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "描绘的场地、空间和个别的动机似乎同时鼓励我们想起像植物、森林、生物、人类这样的动机,同时拒绝最终判断。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "是抽象还是抽象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "福本不太意识到自己的绘画是抽象的,现在也不是“抽象”的立场;与其他画家相比,他对印象主义的克劳德·蒙内和象征主义的奥迪隆·罗登和抽象表达主义的乔恩·米切尔的创作感到同情,但与抽象表达主义的杰克逊·波洛克不同。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/2b57d823/5f04d845-4aec-4553-8df7-29245be39eba.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 成為言語之前 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "當現在福本的創作意識在哪裡,我試圖確定,在本展上發表的作品中,我感覺到其中一大作品在《成為語言之前》(2026)中被凝縮,「生物摩爾菲克」這個詞是值得的,動態的,而且充滿生命力的作品。多重画的屏幕是有效地使用的插入,它的颜色让洞穴的<unk>乳洞的岩皮,而许多其他制作作品让人体的肉块可能让感觉到与自然界的联系,而它的肉感颜色和色彩提醒威廉·德·库宁的“女人”的组合。它看起来像一个女人的胸部,但在母亲的身体里看到婴儿的眼睛也看起来像在生态照片中;看整体,看细节,也变成了一个非常紧张的图像;各种动机被描述为一个神秘的形状,提醒生物和人体的一部分;这部作品也以基于皮肤颜色的颜色绘制,使人体与人体的联系感到强烈。关于这部作品,福本说:“当然,植物,细胞、微生物、生命的生成、变化、从古老到以后的时间等,也引起了兴趣,这部作品在其延伸线上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/4bb2e790/1e8672f9-62bf-4977-a492-7389d53061ae.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 成為語言之前(部分) 2026", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种生命感激的作品也不能无关于近年的经历――即爱情的诞生和成长;从孩子在母亲的身体里时起,可以看到画家的多运感,从孩子在母亲的身体里感觉到它的存在,接受出生和成长作为新体验,并将其提升为形象,在这部作品中可以看到。它将使画家在过去的尝试,以描绘自己的意识作为自然界的一部分,再次迈出一步,更积极地将人类的运作放在画板上,感到新的尝试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/a85f0ee2/81d9f68e-995a-4c47-9c82-c66d5d96a54f.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎《世界一滴之》(AKIINOUE)", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "每個展覽,似乎會感覺到福本以前的運作已經發展得很清楚,顯示的表達的搜尋也感覺得很清楚;製作作品,雖然使用相同的技巧,但有印象表達的表情是多樣的;在未來的創作中,它成為一個展覽,期待它如何發展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "※本稿收集的本书《福本健一郎──世界是一滴的》将于11月底发布。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/0bff6e0a/6fc3b072-d9b2-4da1-aa5f-2c8e6c9efe4d.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "福本健一郎 - 世界一滴", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Reese Witherspoon ‘s Hello Sunshine is majorly shrinking.

Earlier this month, Witherspoon bought her production company back from Candle Media , the Blackstone-backed label that had acquired a controlling stake in 2021. With the support of the French conglomerate Mediawan , the actress was reportedly able to reacquire the banner for just a fraction of the $900 million that Candle Media had paid for it. Now, after just a few weeks in the driver’s seat, Witherspoon has let go some 30 employees — roughly 50% of Hello Sunshine’s staff.

Related Stories

WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role

Here's How to Watch WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Live Online

Variety learned the layoff news from multiple sources, who noted that Hello Sunshine will now focus primarily on film and television projects and the Reese’s Book Club brand, with the direct-to-consumer division being gutted. Reps for Hello Sunshine declined a request for comment.

Though Witherspoon and Mediawan’s control of Hello Sunshine is new, the company is no stranger to layoffs. Under Candle Media’s leadership, it saw at least four rounds of staff reduction in the last two years alone, impacting the unscripted department and the Gen Z-oriented lifestyle brand Sunnie in particular. Candle Media also shuttered Hello Sunshine’s kids and animation unit in 2023. In 2024, it consolidated its live-action division, including that of Hello Sunshine, into Candle Studios, which was led by Hello Sunshine CEO Sarah Harden until she stepped down a year later.

When Witherspoon re-acquired Hello Sunshine, she wrote in a statement that “the best is still ahead.”

“Mediawan has built a global, independent studio by putting creators first. That has always been my vision for Hello Sunshine,” her statement said. “I’m investing alongside Mediawan and joining Pierre-Antoine Capton and his teams because this is the perfect home for this new media landscape. It’s also a homecoming. Peter Chernin and Jesse Jacobs believed in Hello Sunshine from day one. I’m deeply proud of what our incredible team has built, and grateful to Blackstone and Candle Media for their partnership and unwavering support.”

article_text:
Les Innocents de Jack Clayton (1961)

Bien avant que Mike Flanagan n’en tire la série The Haunting of Bly Manor , le célèbre roman de Henry James intitulé Le Tour d’écrou a d’abord donné naissance à un film coécrit par Truman Capote et rebaptisé Les Innocents . Portée par l’excellente Deborah Kerr, cette adaptation retrace l’arrivée d’une gouvernante dans un immense manoir pour s’y occuper de deux charmants orphelins. Très vite néanmoins, elle réalise que les enfants cachent quelque chose, et qu’ils ne sont peut-être pas les seuls habitants de leur grande demeure… Preuve que l’on n’a pas besoin d’effets spéciaux (ni de couleurs) pour faire peur, Les Innocents dialogue avec habilement avec le cinéma gothique et la psychanalyse, et continue de nous hanter bien des années après sa sortie.

The Grudge (呪怨) de Takashi Shimizu (2002)

Impossible de parler de films de fantômes sans mentionner le cinéma japonais, qui, de Hausu à The Ring, nous a donné de quoi faire des cauchemars à vie. A choisir parmi toutes ses productions terrifiantes, on vous conseille The Grudge , l’implacable film de Takashi Shimizu sur une maison hantée pas comme les autres. Troisième adaptation de la même histoire (le réalisateur, motivé par son sujet, avait déjà réalisé deux épisodes sortis directement en DVD), The Grudge a ensuite fait l’objet d’un remake américain -toujours dirigé par Shimizu – avec Sarah Michelle Gellar. Mais ce dernier n’égale en rien l’original, dont les trouvailles visuelles sont aussi malines que glaçantes.

Les Autres d’Alejandro Amenábar (2001)

Landes brumeuses, meubles drapés de blancs, clairs-obscurs menaçants… Formidable tour de force en matière d’ambiance et de suspense, Les Autres fait honneur aux grands manoirs anglais hantés de la plus belle des façons, et ce, bien qu’il ait été tourné en Espagne (le pays d’origine son réalisateur). Hommage réussi aux histoires de fantômes les plus populaires de notre folklore, le film tire sa puissance de la performance inoubliable qu’y livre Nicole Kidman, dont les cheveux blonds soigneusement permanentés et l’effroi nerveux évoquent les meilleures héroïnes hitchcockiennes. A voir, à revoir et à re-revoir jusqu’à s’en faire des nœuds au cerveau.

The Eternal Daughter de Joanna Hogg (2022)

Quoi de mieux que Tilda Swinton tenant le premier rôle dans un film de fantômes ? Tilda Swinton tenant les deux premiers rôles, bien sûr ! Dans ce film de Joanna Hogg, injustement passé inaperçu lors de sa discrète sortie au cinéma en France, l’actrice américaine polymorphe renoue avec le genre fantastique et interprète à la fois la fille et la mère de cette histoire d’épouvante plus envoûtante qu’effrayante. Au programme : un ancien hôtel luxueux, une cinéaste en panne d’inspiration, des souvenirs familiaux déplaisants et, surtout, des images léchées qui témoignent de l’amour que la cinéaste porte à l’imaginaire gothique – et à quel point il est encore possible de nous faire vibrer devant une grande maison dans le brouillard.

A Ghost Story de David Lowery (2017)

Qui a dit que les films de fantômes devaient forcément faire peur ? Certainement pas David Lowery, le réalisateur américain à qui l’on doit ce superbe film où la hantise nous parle surtout de deuil et d’amour déçu. Porté par Rooney Mara et un Casey Affleck difficilement reconnaissable sous son grand drap blanc, A Ghost Story raconte l’errance d’un homme dans la maison qu’il a aimée après qu’un accident lui a ôté la vie. C’est d’une poésie et d’une ingéniosité folles, les images sont superbes, et bien que les frissons ne soient pas au rendez-vous, on vous promet que vous n’en ressortirez pas indemne.

Atlantique de Mati Diop (2019)

Les fantômes ne hantent pas que les grandes maisons victoriennes ou le folklore européen, et la réalisatrice Mati Diop nous l’a rappelé il y’a quelques années en faisant du genre fantastique le somptueux réceptacle d’une réflexion autour de la migration subsaharienne. A travers l’histoire d’amour compliquée entre Ada et Souleiman, deux jeunes sénégalais que la perspective d’un départ pour l’Europe et d’un mariage arrangé menace de séparer, la réalisatrice interroge le vide laissé par les émigrés dans leur société d’origine, ainsi que le destin des femmes qu’ils abandonnent derrière eux. Un premier film stupéfiant et hypnotique, qui fait beaucoup avec peu et s’impose comme l’un des projets les plus marquants du cinéma français contemporain.

Sixième Sens de M. Night Shyamalan (1999)

Si Sixième Sens est de tous les tops, ce n’est pas pour rien. Premier grand succès de M. Night Shyamalan, l’un des réalisateurs horrifiques les plus intéressants (et les plus prolifiques) de notre époque, le film emprunte autant au thriller qu’au genre de l’épouvante, et mise sur une ambiance feutrée, tout en retenue sophistiquée, où les jumpscares n’en sont que plus efficaces. C’est aussi le théâtre de deux performances cultes : d’abord, celle de Bruce Willis dans le rôle d’un psychiatre pour enfants, mais surtout celle de Haley Joel Osment dans celui d’un petit garçon convaincu de voir des fantômes. Point de gothique à l’écran, seulement le Philadelphie huppé des années 90, l’insoutenable irrémédiabilité de la mort et le bruit du silence. C’est déjà pas mal.

▌ À LIRE AUSSI

article_text:
Cheyenne Jackson has acted in more than 40 television series, including “Imperfect Women,” “American Horror Story,” “Call Me Kat,” “Glee” and “30 Rock,” as well as several movies.

But last year, he was close to losing his SAG-AFTRA health insurance because he didn’t meet the qualifying annual minimum of about $28,000 in earnings. The insurance also covers his husband, Jason and their two kids.

ABC Orders Drama Pilot 'Rabbit' Based on U.K. Series 'Ludwig' From Megan Ganz & Humphrey Ker

“I was one gig short of getting my insurance,” Jackson tells me. “We really rely on the SAG insurance. It’s really good.”

He reached out to his friend, “Matlock” star Kathy Bates. He needed to make $6,000.

“I called her, and I was like, ‘Listen, I’m in trouble and I could really use your help. Is there anything I could do on “Matlock”?’” Jackson recalls. “She’s like, ‘Give me a second. Just give me a minute.’”

Bates called him back in less than five minutes. “She’s like, ‘I have good news and bad news for you. The good news is, I got you a role on “Matlock.” The bad news is, you have five lines and you don’t have a name,’” Jackson says. “I was like, ‘Sign me up! No ego amigo here.’ I played no-name detective. I searched a crime scene and I said, ‘Hey, Sergeant, we got some blood over here.’”

View this post on Instagram

Jackson is now paying it forward by launching the “One Job Away” initiative. Started just yesterday, he’s posting headshots and bios on his Instagram feed of actors who are on the verge of losing their SAG-AFTRA health insurance.

With 741,000 Instagram followers, Jackson says he has received “hundreds” of submissions in less than 24 hours. “The bigger conversation is just the way that residuals and SAG are set up,” Jackson says. “I make OK money on residuals, but a lot of that residual does not go toward your SAG dues. You’re essentially starting over every year.”

In other words, Jackson says, “An actor can make $500,000 one year, but when they don’t make much the next year, the $500,000 doesn’t help with the following year’s health insurance minimum.”

He continues, “Journeyman actors and major people who have been the leads of several shows and who have been around for years and years, all of a sudden are, because there are so many fewer jobs and the pay is so much lower, now scrambling for one little guest spot to try to keep their insurance.”

Among the 22 headshots Jackson has posted is Juston Graber, who is just $198.48 shy of qualifying for SAG-AFTRA insurance. Miho Saito is only short $402. Others include Independent Spirit Award nominee Trace Lysette, original “Queer Eye for the Straight Guy” star Jai Rodriguez and Daniel Franzese of “Mean Girls” fame.

Jamie Lee Curtis has reposted some of Jackson’s “One Job Away” posts to her 6.7 million Instagram followers .

Jackson isn’t calling out SAG-AFTRA leadership. “I don’t want to play a blame game,” he says. “What I do want to do is start engaging in a bigger conversation because clearly the system is not working right now.”

“Drake & Josh” actor Drake Bell recently blasted the union after finding out he did not qualify for its insurance.

On his Instagram Story on Oct. 13, Bell posted a screenshot of the SAG-AFTRA health plan website that says, “You do not qualify for Health Plan coverage at this time. Your reported covered earnings from July 2025-June 2026 did not meet minimum eligibility requirements, or you did not qualify other eligibility rules.”

The webpage says that Bell has earned $17,480.53 and that he needs $11,452.47 more to qualify by reaching the $28,933 required for the SAG-AFTRA Health Plan.

Bell wrote over the screenshot, “Do not become an actor. Do not join SAG. You can work for 35 years and they still say [middle finger emoji].”

In September, “Atypical” actor Jack Haven and “Princess Diaries” star Heather Matarazzo both revealed that they wouldn’t qualify for health insurance if they didn’t get more work soon.

title_original: A Palermo c’è una Officina creativa che dialoga con la scena francese
editorial_title_zh: 巴勒莫有一间与法国艺术界对话的创意工坊
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在克卢韦里奥街（via Cluverio）的 Officina：巴勒莫市中心的一家前玻璃厂正让意大利与法国艺术家在设计和实验之间展开对话。“建筑织构”（Architexture）展正以埃尔内斯托·米斯特雷塔（Ernesto Mistretta）和安托尼娜·马伊（Antonina Maj）的展览落下帷幕。文章《巴勒莫有一间创意工坊正……》

article_text:
Si varca la soglia di un’ex vetreria nel centro di Palermo e ci si ritrova immersi in un laboratorio creativo che guarda alla Francia. Questa connessione si esprime appieno in Architexture , rassegna concepita in tre capitoli che da aprile a ottobre vede protagonista l’artista siciliano Ernesto Mistretta . Un percorso iniziato con l’indagine sulla tessitura digitale assieme al duo composto da Edouard Taufenbach e Bastien Pourtout , proseguito attraverso il dialogo con i mobili-scultura firmati dalla direttrice Josephine Flasseur per Officina Allegra , e giunto ora al suo atto conclusivo. Fino al 31 ottobre, presso gli spazi di In via Cluverio, Officina , la mostra Tratto d’unione fa scontrare questa logica con la fisicità delle opere di Antonina Maj .

Ernesto Mistretta e il design digitale in mostra a Palermo

Attraverso l’uso sperimentale di software come AutoCAD, applicando metodologie derivate dall’architettura, Ernesto Mistretta (Marsala, 1976) indaga l’idea di spazio partendo dall’astrazione digitale del pixel. Elemento minimo rielaborato per modularità, ripetizioni e giochi di trasparenza. Oltre a essere artista, è anche architetto e designer, formatosi nello studio parigino di Jean Nouvel . A oggi rinnova i confini disciplinari per approdare alla pittura digitale e propone la costruzione di nuovi mondi visivi.

Dalla riformulazione della texture degli edifici prende il nome l’intera rassegna Architexture . Nell’ambiente espositivo si innesca la dinamica percettiva: il pixel attrae lo sguardo, inducendo a un avvicinamento fisico alla tela mentre la struttura cede a una scomposizione interna che rivela le sue entità mutevoli, frammentate in porzioni infinitesimali. Dopo un’esperienza professionale in Asia, Mistretta afferma di aver ricalibrato il proprio sguardo sull’essenza delle cose, traducendo questa sintesi in un minimalismo formale.

Eppure, se l’eredità del design sopravvive nei criteri di precisione e proporzione, l’espressività delle sue opere resta profondamente legata alla Sicilia. La sua ricerca diventa un tentativo di afferrare il vento, il mare e la luce dell’isola in chiave astratta. L’opera si fa soglia contemplativa e superficie di autoproiezione che offre scenari trasversali in cui riversare il proprio immaginario, che si tratti di ninfee , di uno skyline o di un paesaggio. Un cortocircuito tra spazio mentale e fisico che si fa tangibile nei lavori su specchio, capaci di riflettere e includere l’immagine di chi li osserva.

Antonina Maj e l’archeologia parietale da In via Cluverio, Officina

Diametralmente opposta, ma connessa, è la ricerca di Antonina Maj (Wrocław, 2003). La sua indagine parte dalla materia di un luogo per rivelarne i traumi e le latenze. Artista polacca formatasi all’École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts di Parigi sotto la guida di Tatiana Trouvé , dialoga con le ricerche di Gordon Matta-Clark, Carl Bucher e Simon Hantaï assimilando la loro visione di una superficie da sviscerare.

Attraverso la tecnica del frottage , eseguito sfregando drappi saturi di colore direttamente sulle pareti, Maj cattura l’impronta del luogo. In questo processo, è l’increspatura del tessuto a determinare l’esito visivo, svincolandosi dal controllo preventivo dello sguardo.

Recuperando l’invenzione di Max Ernst , il frottage mantiene la sua matrice surrealista: uno strumento per interrogare le superfici spingendole in una dimensione al di sopra del reale, sospesa tra la memoria dello spazio e nuove possibilità. Nel confronto fisico con i lavori emerge la matericità delle sue opere; le tele cessano di essere semplici supporti bidimensionali per svelare una stratificazione.

Più che imprimere un segno, Maj compie una vera e propria rivelazione in negativo. Un’operazione di scavo e prelievo visivo che genera forme del tutto inedite. I solchi impressi sulle sue tele diventano la cifra stilistica di una ricerca in cui l’architettura cede la propria pelle e la tela ne archivia i segni.

Il dialogo tra Mistretta e Maj chiude la rassegna Architexture

Il Tratto d’unione che dà il titolo alla mostra si materializza in questo scarto continuo tra costruzione formale e indagine stratigrafica. I due artisti sono accomunati dal desiderio di far slittare la percezione del luogo verso territori sconosciuti. Mistretta elabora scenari dall’unità minima del progetto, denaturandola dai suoi valori matematici per sublimare quelli estetici; Maj, al contrario, parte dal dato fisico e architettonico per ricavare una realtà derivata ma parallela.

Il vernissage, animato dalla performance dell’artista Gabrielle Levie in occasione del secondo compleanno della galleria, consolida l’identità dello storico spazio di via Cluverio, confermandolo come una vitale officina di dialogo tra la scena contemporanea italiana e francese.

title_original: U.S. Pavilion at Venice Biennale Is $1 M. Short, and Its Sculptures May Be Stuck in Italy
editorial_title_zh: 美国馆在威尼斯双年展中缺100万美元，其雕塑可能滞留意大利
editorial_excerpt_zh: 尽管争议持续数月，美国设法将阿尔玛·艾伦的雕塑运到了威尼斯。但将其运回家却更加困难。

"translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据《纽约时报》报道，美国艺术保护协会——美国馆的非营利组织——距离筹集展览所需资金还差约100万美元，包括拆除展览和将艺术品运回美国的费用。", "links": [{"text": "The New York Times", "url": "https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/arts/design/us-pavilion-venice-biennale.html"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "美国馆的策展人珍妮·帕里多一直在呼吁潜在的捐助者提供帮助。据《纽约时报》获得的一封信件显示，她承认项目的最后阶段变得困难。", "资金问题为美国在双年展上本已混乱的参与增添了新的篇章。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帕里多此前曾在佛罗里达州经营一家高档宠物店，她被选为美国馆的负责人令人意外。特朗普政府取消了传统的选拔流程，该流程依赖于知名艺术机构的提案和独立评审小组。帕里多在朋友埃琳·斯卡维诺的推荐下获得这份工作，斯卡维诺负责国务院的“外交使团艺术”项目。", "links": [{"text": "scrapped the traditional selection process", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/alma-allens-u-s-pavilion-heads-to-venice-1234781956/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在几位艺术家 reportedly 拒绝了这个机会后，组织者最终选择了居住在墨西哥的美国雕塑家艾伦。从那时起，事情就没有顺利进行。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艾伦告诉《纽约时报》，帕里多和展览策展人杰弗里·乌斯利在展览前都没有参观他的工作室观看这些雕塑。等到威尼斯双年展的预展日结束时，艾伦和乌斯利已经不再交谈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "至于资金困境，艾伦表示他并不了解该非营利组织的筹款情况。他表示，自己的开支仅包括旅行和一间便宜的爱彼迎（Airbnb）住宿，这些费用得到了报销。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最初，主办方将展览的低廉价格标签作为卖点，称这是有史以来最便宜的美国展馆之一。相比之下，2024年的美国展览花费约500万美元，而2022年的展览则接近700万美元。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "国务院为展馆提供了37.5万美元的拨款，其余资金预期由私人捐赠者承担。帕里多的筹款活动包括在迈阿密艺术巴塞尔期间举办的一场派对，以及在马阿拉歌庄园举行的一场晚宴。该部门告诉《纽约时报》，他们并未参与筹款工作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "目前尚不清楚如果帕里多无法填补百万美元的资金缺口会怎样。美国艺术保护协会没有回答《纽约时报》关于如果无法承担将雕塑运回家的费用会采取什么措施的问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾参与组织2017年美国展馆的凯蒂·西格尔对这一情况给出了相当尖锐的评价。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这太疯狂了，”她告诉《纽约时报》。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Despite months of controversy, the United States managed to get Alma Allen ‘s enormous sculptures to Venice for this year’s Biennale. Getting them home, however, is proving more difficult.

The American Arts Conservancy, the nonprofit behind the US Pavilion, is roughly $1 million short of the funds needed to cover the exhibition’s costs, including dismantling the show and shipping the artworks back to the US, according to a report in The New York Times .

Jenni Parido, the pavilion’s commissioner, has been appealing to potential donors for help. In a letter obtained by the Times , she acknowledged that the final stages of the project had become difficult.

“While we have accomplished a tremendous amount in a relatively short period,” Parido wrote, “the final phase of this undertaking has presented financial challenges that I am working tirelessly to resolve.”

The American Arts Conservancy, which Parido runs, has brought in $1.4 million against a projected budget of just under $2.5 million. That shortfall has left it without the funds to store the massive stone and metal sculptures or ship them back to the US. The problem is growing more urgent, as the Biennale is due to close next month. There’s no obvious place nearby to put them, either: the US Pavilion has no storage facilities, and the Guggenheim Foundation, which owns the building, doesn’t have room for them.

The funding troubles add another chapter to what has already been an unusually messy American outing at the Biennale.

Parido, whose previous business experience included running an upscale pet boutique in Florida, was a surprise choice to oversee the US Pavilion. The Trump administration had scrapped the traditional selection process , which relied on proposals from established arts institutions and an independent review panel. Parido got the job after being recommended by her friend Erin Scavino, who heads the State Department’s Art in Embassies program.

The organizers eventually landed on Allen, an American sculptor based in Mexico, after several artists reportedly turned down the opportunity. Things didn’t go smoothly from there.

Allen told the Times that neither Parido nor the exhibition’s curator, Jeffrey Uslip, visited his studio to see the sculptures before the show. By the time the Biennale’s preview days were over, Allen and Uslip were no longer speaking.

As for the financial predicament, Allen said he knew nothing about the nonprofit’s fundraising. His own expenses, he said, amounted to travel and a cheap Airbnb, for which he was reimbursed.

The organizers had initially pitched the exhibition’s modest price tag as a selling point, calling it one of the cheapest US pavilions ever mounted. For comparison, the 2024 American presentation cost about $5 million, while the 2022 edition came in at nearly $7 million.

The State Department provided a $375,000 grant toward the pavilion, with private donors expected to cover the rest. Parido’s fundraising efforts included a party during Art Basel Miami Beach and a dinner at Mar-a-Lago. The department told the Times it wasn’t involved in raising the money.

For now, it’s unclear what happens if Parido can’t close the million dollar gap. The American Arts Conservancy didn’t answer the Times ‘ questions about what it would do if it couldn’t afford to bring the sculptures home.

Katy Siegel, who helped organize the 2017 American pavilion, had a rather pithy assessment of the situation.

“This is crazy,” she told the Times .

title_original: LA SEXTAPE · « The Shards » de Ryan Murphy, le retour du refoulé
editorial_title_zh: 性爱录像带 · 瑞恩·墨菲的《碎片》，被压抑者的回归
editorial_excerpt_zh: 瑞恩·墨菲和布雷特·伊斯顿·埃利斯的这部剧集具备了有罪快感的所有要素：徘徊在高中周边的杀手；荒唐富有且满身可卡因的青少年……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://www.troiscouleurs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/8c44fbde3832df0513dfa10ef11172be-1-1024x576.webp", "alt": "8c44fbde3832df0513dfa10ef11172be 1", "caption": "", "credit": "Trois Couleurs", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "按理说，我本该抗拒。我已经过了那个标准的年纪，我有两个即将步入青春期的女儿，还有一个因长期心情不好而备受磨砺的批判性思维。理性来看，像《碎片》这样的剧集没有任何东西能让我兴奋。然而，我却以一种过夜狂热粉丝那令人尴尬的投入度，一口气刷完了它。瑞恩·墨菲和布雷特·伊斯顿·埃利斯的这部剧集具备了有罪快感的所有要素：徘徊在高中周边的杀手；荒唐富有且满身可卡因的青少年；埃利斯的文字，犹如纵欲后的次日清晨那支冰冷香烟的烟雾般将人包裹。从第一集开始，所有的一切都让我感到羞耻地着迷：吹风造型、游泳池，甚至连地毯也是。吃下蓝色药丸，重新沉浸在九年代那令人安心的母体中，重新变成那个在自己的房间里、伴随着科特·柯本的音乐发现埃利斯的女孩。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "问题是，这个母体本就是一团糟。对我的那代人而言，步入性意识与对艾滋病的恐惧是并存的。渴望，就意味着已经与死亡擦肩而过。再加上一种将虐待进行情色化、将掠夺者视为浪漫形象、将危险视为前戏的文化，你就会得到一个在不知不觉中建立起来的幻想世界，其等式是：性 = 危险 = 死亡。花了二十年去解构它，但神经联结依然还在。正是这个等式让《碎片》再次紧绷。青春期的欲望与徘徊的杀手合二为一。埃利斯从未写过别的东西，掠夺便是欲望的地平线。神来之笔在于选角。苏珊由凯亚·杰柏饰演，她带着母亲辛迪·克劳馥的面容。罗伯特·马洛里由理查·基尔的儿子霍默·基尔饰演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "凯亚的笑容带着一种恐怖谷效应，弗洛伊德称之为“非顺眼感”（“das Unheimliche”，即“恐怖谷”/“奇异陌生感”）：被压抑者的回归。我们看到的不是演员，而是我们复活的偶像，以及那个时代在我们内心植入的一切。英国哲学家马克·费舍称之为“未来的缓慢取消”：一个不再懂得将欲望向前延伸、而是无休止地将其循环往复的时代。甚至在镜头背后，曾出演剧集《欢乐时光》中芳奇尼之子的马克斯·温克勒也在拍摄他曾从内部经历过的那个黄金时代的继承人。这或许就是为什么我没敢承认自己一口气刷完了它。不是因为对某种美学的怀旧，而是出于对当年那个将兴奋与危险混为一谈的青春期自己的羞耻忠诚。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《碎片》，可在 Disney+ 上观看", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "欢迎关注我们", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://www.troiscouleurs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/8c44fbde3832df0513dfa10ef11172be-1-1024x576.webp", "alt": "8c44fbde3832df0513dfa10ef11172be 1", "caption": "", "credit": "Trois Couleurs"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sur le papier, j’aurais dû résister. J’ai passé l’âge canonique, j’ai deux filles bientôt adolescentes et un esprit critique aiguisé par une mauvaise humeur chronique. Rien, rationnellement, ne devrait m’exciter dans une série comme The Shards . Et pourtant, je l’ai bingée avec la dévotion embarrassante d’une groupie d’un soir. La série de Ryan Murphy et Bret Easton Ellis coche toutes les cases du plaisir coupable : un tueur qui rôde autour d’un lycée ; des ados scandaleusement friqués et cocaïnés ; les mots d’Ellis, enveloppant comme la fumée d’une clope froide un lendemain de sexe débridé. Dès le premier épisode, tout m’emballe honteusement : les brushings, les piscines, la moquette même. Prendre la pilule bleue, replonger dans la matrice rassurante des nineties, redevenir celle qui découvrait Ellis dans sa chambre, sur du Kurt Cobain."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sauf que la matrice était fucked up. Pour ma génération, l’entrée dans la sexualité et la terreur du sida allaient de pair. Désirer, c’était déjà côtoyer la mort. Ajoutez-y une culture qui érotisait l’abus, le prédateur en figure romantique, le danger en préliminaire, et vous obtenez un imaginaire bâti, malgré nous, sur une équation : sexe = péril = mort. Vingt ans à la déconstruire, mais le câblage, lui, tient toujours. C’est cette équation que The Shards remet sous tension. Le désir adolescent et le tueur qui rôde ne font qu’un. Ellis n’a jamais écrit autre chose, la prédation comme horizon du désir. Le coup de génie est dans le casting. Susan, c’est Kaia Gerber, affichant le visage de sa mère, Cindy Crawford. article_text:
Sur le papier, j’aurais dû résister. J’ai passé l’âge canonique, j’ai deux filles bientôt adolescentes et un esprit critique aiguisé par une mauvaise humeur chronique. Rien, rationnellement, ne devrait m’exciter dans une série comme The Shards . Et pourtant, je l’ai bingée avec la dévotion embarrassante d’une groupie d’un soir. La série de Ryan Murphy et Bret Easton Ellis coche toutes les cases du plaisir coupable : un tueur qui rôde autour d’un lycée ; des ados scandaleusement friqués et cocaïnés ; les mots d’Ellis, enveloppant comme la fumée d’une clope froide un lendemain de sexe débridé. Dès le premier épisode, tout m’emballe honteusement : les brushings, les piscines, la moquette même. Prendre la pilule bleue, replonger dans la matrice rassurante des nineties, redevenir celle qui découvrait Ellis dans sa chambre, sur du Kurt Cobain.

Sauf que la matrice était fucked up. Pour ma génération, l’entrée dans la sexualité et la terreur du sida allaient de pair. Désirer, c’était déjà côtoyer la mort. Ajoutez-y une culture qui érotisait l’abus, le prédateur en figure romantique, le danger en préliminaire, et vous obtenez un imaginaire bâti, malgré nous, sur une équation : sexe = péril = mort. Vingt ans à la déconstruire, mais le câblage, lui, tient toujours. C’est cette équation que The Shards remet sous tension. Le désir adolescent et le tueur qui rôde ne font qu’un. Ellis n’a jamais écrit autre chose, la prédation comme horizon du désir. Le coup de génie est dans le casting. Susan, c’est Kaia Gerber, affichant le visage de sa mère, Cindy Crawford. Robert Mallory, c’est Homer Gere, fils de Richard.

Le sourire de Kaia est une uncanny valley, « das Unheimliche » (« l’inquiétante étrangeté ») disait Freud : le refoulé qui fait retour. Nous ne regardons pas des acteurs mais nos idoles ressuscitées, et tout ce que leur époque avait implanté en nous. Le philosophe britannique Mark Fisher appelait cela la « lente annulation du futur » : une époque qui, ne sachant plus tracer son désir vers l’avant, en refait indéfiniment la boucle. Jusque derrière la caméra, où Max Winkler, fils du Fonzie de la série Happy Days, filme les héritiers d’un âge d’or qu’il a connu de l’intérieur. Voilà peut-être pourquoi je l’ai bingée sans oser l’avouer. Pas par nostalgie d’une esthétique, mais par fidélité honteuse à l’ado que j’étais, celle qui confondait l’excitation et le péril.

article_text:
The ICP Museum in New York presents “I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now,” an exhibition organized by Aperture that brings together twenty-eight artists of different generations, from postwar Japan to the present day.

By Gaia Squarci. Cover photo by Asako Narahashi.

The story of Japanese photography has mostly been told through men, though countless women helped shape it and remain largely overlooked. Curated by Pauline Vermare, Lesley A. Martin, and Takeuchi Mariko, the exhibition grew out of Aperture’s 2024 book and its accompanying show at the Rencontres d’Arles. At ICP, the installations are as varied as the artists themselves. Three threads run through the work: close observation of everyday life, critical takes on the social roles Japanese women inhabit and reinvent, and experiments that push photography beyond its usual limits.

Asako Narahashi shoots from the surface of the water. Her images float between freedom and fear, as if the viewer could rise above the waves or sink beneath them at any moment. Miyako Ishiuchi’s Mother’s (2000–2005) unfolds as an intimate observation of the possessions her late mother left behind: lingerie, faded photographs, worn-down lipsticks. The series suggests that what we own may become the way we are remembered.

Hitomi Watanabe takes the visitor into the streets of Shinjuku, the heart of Tokyo’s 1960s counterculture. She photographed as an insider of the Zenkyoto student movement, which occupied the University of Tokyo campus in 1968–69 to demand academic reform and political change, and her images capture both the struggle and the everyday life of the protesters. These and many other bodies of work are a reminder that Japanese women photographers have been producing daring and intimate images for decades, largely outside the spotlight.

The exhibition “I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now” is on view at The International Center of Photography (ICP) in New York City until January 11, 2027.

article_text:
The Hong Foundation was founded in 1971 by Hong Chien Chuan, who established the National brand of home electronics in Taiwan, and later Panasonic Taiwan. The foundation runs a series of prizes and projects, and supports various cultural practitioners both on individual projects and through the development of their careers. It launched a contemporary art programme in 2014 under Grace Cheung, the founding principal of XRANGE Architects and executive director of the Hong Foundation.

ArtReview The Hong Foundation dates back to 1971: how and why was it founded?

Grace Cheung The foundation was founded when Taiwan was still under martial law and dominated by strongman politics. As you can imagine, back in the 1970s, in Taiwan there wasn’t what you might call a literary scene, let alone an art scene. A lot of the philanthropy back then took the form of charities helping people without the means to navigate basic necessities. We were the first foundation to be set up with the express purpose of supporting education for arts and culture, and remained distinct in our commitment to education. That has been what has set us apart all these years. In November, we will be 55 years old.

AR Do you think the mission has changed over the course of that history?

GC I believe for our foundation to still be able to do the work it does, change is inevitable. With new ideas and new people, you look for the best way to move forward in any current situation. To give you an example, in the 1970s, there were no children’s books written by local writers, or the telling of local stories. A lot of the history and the culture is oral. Our foundation started a children’s literature prize. We found writers and illustrators, and essentially built up children’s literature. We were also the first to sponsor Cloud Gate Dance Theatre’s Lin Hwai-min when he just started out in the 1970s. Our executive director, Celia Hong, who is also my mother-in-law, always tells this story of when he would come to the foundation just wearing flip-flops and a pair of shorts and nothing else. This became a long-term relationship, with us sponsoring them over 14 productions. These were instances of support for culture where there was none. I became involved with the foundation by starting the visual art programme 12 years ago; it was a completely new thing.

AR Why support visual arts, rather than, say, your own discipline – architecture?

GC I have been interested in art ever since I was a child. When I was six, I really thought I wanted to be an artist. This fire has always been inside. When I began to participate in the foundation, I thought looking into art would be a really great way to engage, to learn something new and get refreshed from architecture. Over the years, this has become a really great balance for me personally: I have the professional architecture side, where it’s always busy with projects. Then on the art side, I can take a different angle, searching for artists and creative people that resonate with me, and then to try and support them on their journey.

AR What kind of thing resonates with you? Would you ever support an artist whose work you really didn’t like?

GC I think if you don’t like the work, it’s hard to feel like you want to be a part of it. Maybe it has to do with an important or a relevant issue, but if I don’t like how they tell the story, or the artistic means they chose, or if I think it could be done in a better way, then something is missing. Finding the resonance is a really abstract, but highly visceral thing.

AR Do you get a sense of the kind of things you’re going to be attracted to?

GC Yes, I do. I think my art-history and architecture-school training gives me a good understanding. When I encounter an artist, I always like to know where they’re coming from: what propels you? What is the artistic means? I think I can tell when I look at a piece how difficult it is to produce and to edit conceptually. How difficult it is to combine the two into something completely new. I’m often not satisfied if it’s just about beauty. How deeply does it connect? What is the cosmic story, where is that spark? I think I look for that.

AR Does that extend to particular mediums like video or photography?

GC I’m pretty open with all types of mediums: it could be from graffiti to machines to oil painting, mixed media, video, etc. I don’t think the medium matters that much. I think what I look for first and foremost is the story, and the person, because it is a long-term relationship that I’m interested in. I never believe that one particular work can represent someone’s entire career. Artists don’t work like that, and the same is true of the foundation. Historically, we have been doing things long-term. The children’s literature programme ran for 18 years; our support for Cloud Gate went on for 20 years. Now these projects are self-sustaining and don’t need our support anymore.

AR Do you know when they reach that moment?

GC They come to you less and less. Then there will be a time when they come and ask for your help to support just a portion of a project. That’s why part of our art programme is structured like that: we have what we call the extension project, for artists that we work with long-term, so that from time to time when they do a project and they’re short that bit of funding, then we can come in and support. It really depends on what they need. Luckily, Taiwanese artists are generally quite humble and they’re not greedy. Long-term, it really does become a trust relationship. It’s really great to be there and see how their work transforms, seeing the success that they have and then still being able to lend a hand whenever they need it. Being an artist, it’s extremely difficult to survive, even though, I think, making art is one of the most important pursuits for human beings.

AR What is it, do you think, that art, and culture more generally, bring that is so important?

GC I feel like it’s an innate human longing to want to have that special spark. You could think back to cavemen making handprints and then varying the sizes, the colours. It’s playful, even useless, but it gives a lot of pleasure. Through that pleasure, you reflect on a lot of things. Building, let’s say, hospitals – those are important, but what makes the patient happy in the hospital? Perhaps it’s just a really beautiful drawing. I think that art still has that ability, it’s as important as sustenance in a way. It’s basic and it breaks down all barriers without language faster and easier than anything we’ve got.

AR How much do you think the foundation’s activities are tied to an idea of nation-building for Taiwan, and supporting the development of a particularly Taiwanese type of art?

GC I’d be lying if I said the foundation was completely independent of that. If you look back, my husband’s family has been in Taiwan for nine generations. It’s always been an unspoken understanding that we will support talents and ideas from Taiwan. It’s not intentionally political. I find it much easier, much more direct that we focus locally. It’s ultimately the goal.

AR At the same time, a lot of the artists and projects you support are not only located in Taiwan anymore: you work, for example, with Dia in the US and the Rijksakademie in the Netherlands. How does that support your goal?

GC Taiwan is a very small place, but we’ve had a high proportion of good artists working in different genres and with great diversity. I think we’re quite lucky with that. We started collaborating internationally last year because I’m really interested in giving these artists the training and the exposure that they need to become better artists. For example, with the Rijksakademie, the education that they provide would be impossible in Taiwan: for us to replicate it would cost an insane amount of money, a lot of red tape, and would perhaps be extremely difficult to kickstart and sustain. It’s much easier to work with Rijks. If there is a Taiwanese artist that makes the cut there, then we will definitely come in and support.

With Dia, Hsieh Tehching started out as an artist when we founded our foundation. Of course, Hsieh Tehching considers himself an American artist with Taiwanese roots, but he’s still highly revered in Taiwan. That’s why it was a project that we wanted to get involved in, and recap on his inimitable life’s work in a sense.

AR Is that indicative of some of the changes that have happened with the times since the foundation began? In the sense that the idea of ‘Taiwanese’ art is now something that exists on a more international plane, in the context of a diaspora, for example, than it may have when the foundation began.

GC When I look at the artists from Taiwan, I also want to see that they’re not trapped in a Taiwanese identity. They need to be able to tell their story, but in a way that can resonate with as many people as possible. To do that, you have to actually go down to a deeper human level. For example, you can be very political, but you don’t have to flash national flags. There are ways to describe these very complex situations and emotions without going there. I believe the artists that we have supported are all capable of doing that.

AR What does success look like? When you have a project, that it gets shown in a museum or a biennial, or that the artist you support just makes their work?

GC I use myself as the first hurdle. When I support an artist and then I see the work and I’m genuinely impressed and blown away, that is success. Because if we hadn’t supported the artists, they would not have been able to make these works. Then there are pieces that are really stunning, where artists have broken through their own barriers, beyond what they usually do, and moved forward conceptually. If I see that the artist actually managed to break free of whatever limitation, some kind of glass wall or ceiling, then I would also say that is success. In our experience, these pieces would then get exhibited elsewhere, outside of Taiwan, because they are really that good. That is also success.

AR Does the foundation have a collection?

GC Previously, when we commissioned all the work, we didn’t seek to collect it because we didn’t have the space. We just recently changed our by-laws so that we can now take on a collection. We’re also just starting the process of building our own building. Through this, I want to start commissioning more artists to put work in situ, so that the commissioned work is embedded with the building, in the building material, in the spaces.

AR Given the developments of new technologies, and AI in particular, is this something that you feel might change the purpose of the foundation?

GC We are testing how we can have a relationship with AI. We have sponsored artists looking into AI previously. Li Yi-Fan, when he won our award, my condition for him was to look into AI. To use his crazy logic to look into this and to tease out some issues, because I know he will use it smartly, not in a dumb way to just generate a lot of smooth AI images. This is still in progress. We’ve also recently commissioned a young artist, a recent graduate, Chang Shu-Wei, exploring this idea of AI companions. I am interested in seeing how artists might use their own creativity to respond to AI. It’s part tool, part database, but not exactly a producer. I am interested in artistic practice that is not drowned by AI but still maintains the human quality above all, that could navigate this very fine line to look for that really unique take. In short, I won’t say no to AI, but I’m very critical.

With the foundation, the way we sponsor artists, a lot of it is really trial and error. The best way really is to learn by doing. We really believe that culture can generate industry. This is an issue that we are very interested in.

AR Would this be a new programme that you would introduce into the foundation’s mission?

GC If there is an opportunity, we are very open to doing that. When we have our own building, I won’t say no to, for example, starting a small production arm. It just takes one opportunity where this could work, and then it could generate new things. We own, on the one hand, quite a few companies. We also have investment companies that generate income to support the foundation. Then, in turn, the foundation can support the kind of cultural production that eventually could become an industry. We are very interested in seeing how it could come full circle. We’ve done a lot of pairings for artists, connecting them with the larger business network to help them with their research. So far, there hasn’t been a moment where we could, say, embed an artist somewhere or have an artist collaborate with business yet. The final goal is to grow a new type of artist, if you will. A completely new form of practice. How exciting the world would be if there were no such categorisations about what, say, an architect can do, what an artist can do, but that someone trained in either discipline can be generally a creative problem-solver. I think that would be the day we really succeeded.

article_text:
中国語の歌を190年ぶりに披露

忘れもしない2019年10月の火災から7年。復元された首里城正殿の一般公開が11月23日に迫る中、首里城を臨む人工の池、那覇市の龍潭(りゅうたん)で7日夕方、「御冠船ハーリーとライトアップ点灯式」が行われました。池の奥に見えるのが首里城正殿です。

琉球王国時代、中国から派遣された冊封使をもてなすために龍潭で行われたのが「御冠船ハーリー」。地元のNPO法人首里まちづくり研究会が、過去の記録や研究をもとに歌詞などをできる限り再現しました。

元になったのは1838年に開催された「重陽宴」の記録。日記にある中国語のハーリー歌は旋律や発音が不明でしたが、一部が那覇市久米で歌い継がれているハーリー歌と合致することが分かりました。今回は現代の普通語に近い発音で歌いました。

幻想的なライトアップも必見！

ライトアップの際は琉球古典音楽を披露。幻想的な光景と典雅な歌唱に歓声が上がりました。

大国の狭間で生き抜いてきた琉球王国。現代にも繋がる歴史の厚みと当時の人々の営みを感じさせる、有意義な再現イベントでした。

歴史の舞台である龍潭も、首里城正殿の復元を機に改めて注目したいスポットです。ライトアップは2027年2月27日（日）まで。午後6時～午後10時に点灯します。

首里城見学とあわせてオススメです。（美術展ナビ編集班 岡部匡志）

article_text:
Michelle Hooper is leaving Searchlight Pictures as executive vice president of marketing after two decades with the company.

Since joining in 2006, Hooper’s work on publicity, awards and creative marketing helped earn the studio nearly 200 Oscar nominations and more than 130 Golden Globe nominations. Of those 200, Searchlight took home 49 wins, including best picture winners “Nomadland,” “The Shape of Water,” “Birdman,” “12 Years a Slave” and “Slumdog Millionaire.” Searchlight also received best picture nominations at the Golden Globes for the aforementioned titles, in addition to 15 others.

Related Stories

Ava DuVernay’s Doc ‘14th’ to Submit New Original Song by Brittany Howard and Robert Glasper for Oscars Consideration (EXCLUSIVE)

Olivia Wilde Eyes Oscars History With 'The Invite' as the First Woman to Direct Herself to an Acting Nomination

This awards season, Hooper was leading campaigns for “Wild Horse Nine” and “Behemonth!,” among other titles.

“She’s a stellar leader for her creative insights and keen ability to read a film for where it fits in the zeitgeist, in turn setting her team up for wide-reaching success,” said a longtime colleague. “But she’s also an equally formidable collaborator, one who can close a campaign with all the insights gained from keeping her ear to the ground and hearing feedback in real time. It’s a loss for the studio, but I guarantee you it will be another’s gain.”

Earlier in her career, Hooper worked at CBS Entertainment as the director of entertainment communications and aided in the “Survivor” publicity strategy; she also spent four years at Fox Broadcast as the company’s VP of entertainment publicity, where she worked on campaigns for shows like “The Simpsons,” “Arrested Development” and “American Idol.”

Hooper was featured in Variety ’s 2025 Women’s Impact Report alongside fellow Searchlight executives Rebecca Kearey, DanTram Nguyen and Katie Goodson-Thomas, whose work to ensure the studio had a stellar year at the Oscars was highlighted.

“The team’s marketing mojo led to 10 Academy Award nominations for ‘A Complete Unknown’ and ‘A Real Pain,’ including a best supporting actor win for Kieran Culkin’s performance in the Jesse Eisenberg film,” wrote Variety.

In a joint statement, the team explained that Searchlight’s adventurous choices and deep filmmaker relationships help the company weather the challenges of the business by “trusting [that] audiences still want films that entertain, challenge and provoke.”
